Tool Library Opens Two-Week Return Period With No Charges
Overdue equipment accepted at the counter, with borrowing rights restored
PEMBERTON (March 3) — The Pemberton Community Tool Library will accept overdue equipment without charge from March 16 through March 27. Late fees of 40 cents per day already recorded on those loans will be canceled for any item handed back within that period.
Records show that many membership accounts have not been able to take out equipment, because tools borrowed last season were never returned. --[1]--. Once the missing item is checked in, the restriction is removed the same day.
--[2]--. Items must be handed to staff at the service counter while the counter is open. --[3]--. The unattended after-hours return slot may not be used during this period, because each tool is inspected as it is received.
"Every ladder or sander left in a garage is one that another member cannot borrow, and our volunteers can check in only so many items each evening," said Ivan Lindqvist, equipment program coordinator.
Powered garden machinery and any item outstanding for more than 180 days remain subject to the usual daily charge. --[4]--.
Questions may be directed to 555-0142. The counter is staffed from 10 A.M. to 6 P.M., Tuesday through Saturday.

Rating: 4 out of 5

Account type: Business (verified)

Nothing I read before booking told me where the limits of this arrangement lie, so I am setting them out here.
Our lease ended nine weeks before the new floor was ready, and buying desks we would then store would have cost more than hiring. We took 24 pieces. Delivery staff removed the protective covers on arrival.
The desks and seating were sound. The three storage cabinets, though, were too shallow to hold our files upright. An exchange must be requested while at least fourteen days of the term remain, and we were inside that window, so I asked for deeper units. They arrived four days later rather than the next working day. I claimed nothing off the invoice and booked a second short hire in February.
The total came to $2,150, which our relocation budget
covered
easily, though delivery and collection are billed separately and the rate list does not say so.

Does not suit: teams with unusual storage needs, or terms under three weeks.

Graham Purcell (2:07 P.M.): Back. Two conditions apply before we can accept water. First, it has to reach one of our sites within eight hours of being taken. Second, every bottle has to be sealed and marked with the time of collection. Neither applies here.
Marisol Cadena (2:12 P.M.): I'll ask for a fresh set first thing tomorrow, and mailing them is not an option. [Call logged under reference NR-2408.]

To: Mr. Douglas Peralta
From: Repairs Counter, Mowbray Works
Date: March 20
Subject: Result of your purchase protection claim
Claim reference: RC-5140
Thank you for leaving your machine with us on March 12 with your completed claim form. You mentioned then that you plan to travel to work on it each morning once it is returned.
The rear hub has failed and no longer turns freely. The rim above it is bent and several spokes are loose. The saddle and the handlebar grips show ordinary wear only, and the helmet you left with the machine is undamaged.
Covered by the plan: a new rear hub, supplied and fitted at no charge.
Not covered by the plan: straightening the rim and replacing spokes, $58.00, of which $19.00 is workshop labor.
We forwarded our findings to the maker's support office, which has ruled that a hub failure of this kind falls inside the plan but impact damage to a rim does not. The replacement hub came from our regional stock depot and is already here. Your purchase record was already on file, so we did not need to ask you for it.
Please approve the second line in writing before we begin the work. We can hold the machine for ten days. Without a reply by March 30, you will need to collect it unrepaired. We will also check the seat height at no charge before the machine leaves us. You will find our counter beside the luggage shop.
Ellis Karvonen
Repairs Counter, Mowbray Works
P.S. We will take care of the labor portion shown on the second line ourselves, as the machine has waited here longer than we promised.

The late evening slot suited us
Rating: 5 out of 5 — service used: out-of-hours carpet cleaning
Colin Radcliffe, owner of a toy shop, Norbury district
Our shop closes at eight, and I did not want machines running around customers, so I chose the later evening time. I let the crew in myself at nine and came back at 12:30 to lock up after them. Our unit sits above a bakery and has no elevator, so the crew carried every machine up two flights from the street, and work on the carpet still began before ten.
They worked around the display shelves with real care, and nothing was marked. That is not the main reason we changed suppliers, though. The company we used last year told us to clear the floor ourselves before each visit, which kept two of my staff late the night before. This crew moves the furniture out and puts it back as part of the job.
Would book again: Yes
